learn.title: What is perimeter?
learn.html:
The perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape.

Imagine an ant 🐜 walking along every side of the triangle and back to the start. The distance it walks is the perimeter.

Perimeter of a triangle = side + side + side

learn.title: Equilateral triangle ABC
learn.html:
Each side is 15 cm.

Perimeter = 15 + 15 + 15 = 45 cm

learn.title: Finding a missing side
learn.html:
If you know the perimeter and 2 sides:

Missing side = perimeter - the 2 sides you know

learn.title: Related rectangle
learn.html:
Draw a rectangle around a triangle so they share the same base and height. This is the triangle's related rectangle.

The triangle is always half of its related rectangle.

learn.title: Rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm
learn.html:
Area of rectangle = 6 × 4 = 24 cm²

Triangle ACD is half of it: ½ × 24 = 12 cm²

Count the squares to check: whole squares and half squares make 12 ✓

learn.title: The area formula
learn.html:
Area of triangle = ½ × base × height

The height must meet the base at a right angle. It can be a side, a dashed line inside, or even a dashed line outside the triangle.

learn.title: Triangle ABC
learn.html:
Base = 4 cm, height = 3 cm.

Area = ½ × 4 × 3 = ½ × 12 = 6 cm²

learn.title: Height outside the triangle
learn.html:
Base KL = 7 cm. The height is the dashed line, 16 cm. It is outside the triangle, but it still meets the base line at a right angle.

Area = ½ × 7 × 16 = ½ × 112 = 56 cm²

learn.title: Shaded parts
learn.html:
Sometimes the shaded part is not a triangle.

Shaded area = whole shape - the part that is not shaded

learn.title: ABCD is a rectangle
learn.html:
Area of rectangle = 12 × 8 = 96 cm²

White triangle DEC = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm²

Shaded part = 96 - 48 = 48 cm²

questions.label: Do and Learn 1

questions.hint: Count squares. Each square is 1 cm. Count the base along the bottom and the height straight up.
steps: The base is 8 cm. Count the squares from C to B: 8.
The height is 6 cm. It meets the base at a right angle. Count the squares from the base straight up to A: 6.
Area of triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6
questions.why: The triangle is half of a 8 by 6 rectangle.

learn.title: Solving word problems
learn.html:
1. Read and draw a picture.

2. Is it asking for perimeter (distance around) or area (space inside)?

3. Write the numbers on the picture.

4. Calculate and write the unit: cm or m for perimeter, cm² or m² for area.

learn.title: Lily's triangular wood
learn.html:
Lily paints a triangular piece of wood with base 32 cm and height 26 cm. What area does she paint?

Area = ½ × 32 × 26 = ½ × 832 = 416 cm²

learn.title: A missing side
learn.html:
A tile has perimeter 48 cm. Two sides are 16 cm and 12 cm.

16 + 12 = 28. The third side = 48 - 28 = 20 cm.

learn.title: Tom's triangular scarf
learn.html:
Tom's scarf has sides 1.2 m, 0.8 m and 0.8 m. Perimeter in cm?

1.2 + 0.8 + 0.8 = 2.8 m = 2.8 × 100 = 280 cm

learn.title: Two ways to find a shaded area
learn.html:
Add the pieces together, or

find the whole shape and take away the white part.

learn.title: Area of the field PTRS
learn.html:
Way 1: square 6 × 6 = 36 m², triangle ½ × 4 × 6 = 12 m², 36 + 12 = 48 m²

Way 2: rectangle 10 × 6 = 60 m², white triangle 12 m², 60 - 12 = 48 m²

questions.label: Do and Learn 1
questions.q: Alex cut a piece of paper into an isosceles triangle. Its perimeter is 46.5 cm. If the adjacent sides to the vertex are 14.5 cm each, what is its base?
questions.hint: The 2 sides next to the vertex are equal (14.5 cm each). The base is what is left of the perimeter.
questions.why: The 3 sides must add up to 46.5 cm.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2
questions.q: Marvin cut out the orange triangle from the rectangular piece of paper shown. What is the area of the orange triangle?
questions.hint: Use the short side on BC as the base. The height is the length of the rectangle.
steps: BC is 10 cm long (the same as AD). The bottom part of BC is 6 cm.
So the base of the orange triangle (on BC) = 10 - 6 = 4 cm.
The height goes from D straight across to BC: 15 cm.
questions.why: The orange triangle has base 4 cm on BC and height 15 cm.

questions.hint: An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides. Add all 3 sides.
steps: The 3 sides are 36.5 cm, 22.5 cm and 22.5 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q: The floor pattern of a room is as shown below. What is the area of the green part?
questions.hint: Use EG as the base (count the squares down). The height goes across to F.
steps: Each square is 1 cm. The base EG goes down the left side: count 7 squares, so 7 cm.
The height goes from the line EG straight across to F: count 9 squares, so 9 cm.
questions.why: The green triangle EFG has base 7 cm and height 9 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 3

questions.hint: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.q: Jaden owns a land in the shape of an isosceles triangle. Its perimeter is 96 m. If one of the non-identical sides of the land is 34 m, what are the lengths of the other two sides?
questions.hint: The other 2 sides are the same length. Take away 34 m, then share what is left equally.
steps: An isosceles triangle has 2 sides the same length. The 34 m side is the different one.
questions.why: The 2 equal sides share the 62 m: 31 + 31 = 62.

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.q: A land in the shape of a rectangle was divided into 3 parts as shown below. What is the area of Part B?
questions.hint: Part B's base is the whole bottom of the rectangle. Its height is the width of the rectangle.
steps: The bottom of the rectangle = 28 + 9 = 37 m. This is the base of Part B.
The height of Part B = the width of the rectangle = 24 m.
questions.why: Part B has base 37 m and height 24 m.

questions.label: Exercise 6
questions.q: The figure ABCD is made up of two different triangles. ABD is a right triangle. AB = 25 cm, AD = 60 cm, BD = 65 cm and CE = 45 cm. Find the area of figure ABCD. Find the perimeter of triangle ABD.
questions.hint: Find each triangle's area and add them. For BCD, BD is the base and CE is the height.
steps: Triangle ABD: base AD = 60 cm, height AB = 25 cm.
Triangle BCD: base BD = 65 cm, height CE = 45 cm.
questions.answer: Area of ABCD = 2,212.5 cm², perimeter of ABD = 150 cm
questions.why: The figure is 2 triangles added together.

questions.label: Exercise 7
questions.q: In the figure, ACEF is a rectangle and BC = CD = DE. The area of rectangle ACEF is 80 cm². Find the area of the triangle BDF.
questions.hint: First find the width CE. Then find the 3 white triangles and take them away from 80 cm².
steps: The length FE is 10 cm. Width CE = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 cm.
CD = DE and CD + DE = 8, so CD = DE = 4 cm. BC = CD, so BC = 4 cm.
questions.why: 80 cm² minus the white triangles (24 + 8 + 20 = 52 cm²) leaves 28 cm².

questions.label: Exercise 8
questions.q: Janice place 2 tiles next to each other to create a pattern. What is the area of the orange part?
questions.hint: Add the 2 squares. Then take away the 2 white triangles.
steps: White triangle PRS: base PR = 40 + 25 = 65 cm, height RS = 25 cm. Area = ½ × 65 × 25 = 812.5 cm²
questions.why: The 2 squares (2,225 cm²) minus the 2 white triangles (1,612.5 cm²).

learn.title: Unit 9 big ideas
learn.html:
Perimeter = add all 3 sides (cm, m).

Area = ½ × base × height (cm², m²).

The height meets the base at a right angle. It can be outside the triangle.

learn.title: Square numbers help
learn.html: If a square has area 100 cm², its side is the number that times itself makes 100: 10 × 10 = 100, so 10 cm.

learn.title: Math in Real Life (p.104)
learn.html:
A right triangle has sides 3 cm and 4 cm at the right angle. The long side is 5 cm, because 3 × 3 + 4 × 4 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5 × 5.

Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm. Area = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 cm².

questions.label: Let's Think Along
questions.q: Ravi is given 2 squares, A and B. He covers ½ of the small square with the big square as shown to make Figure C. Find the area of Figure C.
questions.hint: Draw the 2 diagonals of the big square. It splits into 4 identical triangles. The uncovered part D is one of them.
steps: The 2 diagonals of square B cut it into 4 identical triangles. The uncovered part D is the same size as one of them.
Area of triangle D = ¼ of 64 = 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm²
questions.why: Figure C is the big square plus the uncovered triangle D.

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: Figure A is a right triangle with base 6 cm and height 8 cm. 4 of these right triangles are arranged and pasted on a piece of paper to form Figure B as shown below. What is the length of each side of the big square in Figure B?
questions.hint: Find the small square in the middle first. Then add up all the pieces to get the big square's area.
steps: The small square in the middle has side 8 - 6 = 2 cm. Its area = 2 × 2 = 4 cm²
Each right triangle = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm². 4 triangles = 4 × 24 = 96 cm²
Which number times itself makes 100? 10 × 10 = 100. So each side is 10 cm.
questions.why: The big square is 4 triangles (96 cm²) and the small square (4 cm²): 100 cm² = 10 cm × 10 cm.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle and EBD is a triangle. Describe two methods to find the area of the shaded triangle.
questions.hint: One method uses taking away. The other uses the triangle formula.
steps: Method 1: Find the area of rectangle ABCD. Then subtract the areas of triangles AED and BCD.
Method 2: Use area of triangle = ½ × base × height.
The base is BE. The height is AD (it meets the line AB at a right angle).
Area of triangle EBD = ½ × BE × AD
questions.answer: Method 1: rectangle ABCD - triangle AED - triangle BCD. Method 2: ½ × BE × AD
questions.why: Both methods give the same area.
